redundancy.implication: one is very likely derived from the other; do not treat as independent evidence

ideas.title: Is the absent arm effect a true null, or an insensitive test?
ideas.question: arm showed no detectable difference in post_score. Is that evidence of no effect, or evidence that this sample could not have detected a clinically meaningful one? What is the smallest effect these data can exclude?

evidence.detail: arm ~ post_score is not among the confirmed or raw-significant pairs; check the scan inventory for its exact estimate

ideas.estimand: the confidence interval for the arm effect, and the equivalence bound the data can support

analysis.method: report the CI and MDE; equivalence/non-inferiority test against a margin the user sets
tasks: equivalence test against the chosen margin
state what can and cannot be excluded

ideas.falsification: the CI excludes effects larger than the equivalence margin (then the null is informative)
ideas.caveat: this reframes a null as a bounded estimate; it cannot prove absence of effect, only exclude effects larger than the bound

ideas.title: Where is the decision threshold, and how certain are we about it?
ideas.question: If a decision is made from post_score, where is the threshold of practical consequence, how many cases sit near it, and how much would better measurement move them across it?
ideas.estimand: probability of crossing a decision-relevant threshold, by group; threshold sensitivity

analysis.method: threshold analysis / expected-value of information; ROC or CDF near the cut
tasks: define the threshold with the user

ideas.falsification: no plausible threshold exists, or all cases are far from it
ideas.caveat: the threshold is a value judgement supplied by the user; do not invent it

power.note: focus is precision near the threshold

ideas.title: Does arm change the adherence → post_score association?
ideas.question: For whom, or under what conditions, does adherence predict post_score? Is the effect stronger at some levels of arm — and is the interaction large enough to matter?
ideas.estimand: interaction coefficient for adherence × arm on post_score

analysis.method: moderated regression, simple slopes at mean ±1 SD, Johnson-Neyman

ideas.caveat: each additional moderator is a test; more than 2-3 candidates requires FDR correction and a theoretical reason for each
assumption_risks: interaction tests need ~4x the N of a main effect for the same power

ideas.title: Can post_score be predicted well enough to be useful?
ideas.question: Forgetting explanation for a moment: how accurately can post_score be predicted from the available variables, out of sample — and is that accurate enough to support a decision?

analysis.method: penalised regression with repeated cross-validation; calibration; no p-values

ideas.falsification: out-of-sample AUC CI includes 0.5 (no better than chance)
ideas.caveat: events per variable ≈ 34.2; below 10 the model is over-parameterised. Prediction and explanation answer different questions — do not report these coefficients as effects

power.note: prediction uses precision (CI width), not power

assumption_risks: education has few integer levels: decide ordinal vs continuous explicitly
satisfaction has few integer levels: decide ordinal vs continuous explicitly

ideas.title: Is the age → post_score relation non-linear (threshold or U-shaped)?
ideas.question: The association between age and post_score is not monotonic across quintiles. Is there a threshold or an optimal range, and where?

evidence.detail: quintile means: 24.81, 25.58, 22.22, 22.82, 27.97 — non-monotonic: the association changes direction or is U-shaped
the linear association was NOT FDR-confirmed; curvature needs a theoretical reason

ideas.estimand: the shape of E[outcome | exposure]: slope below vs above a breakpoint, or the optimal range

analysis.method: quadratic/spline model, segmented regression for a breakpoint with CI

ideas.falsification: the curvature term is not significant and the linear fit is adequate
ideas.caveat: the linear association itself was not significant after FDR — this idea is a specification check, not a follow-up to a confirmed effect; it will often return a flat curve

ideas.title: Does post_score change over time — and is the change real?
ideas.question: Does post_score trend, cycle, or step-change across enrol_date? Is any apparent change distinguishable from seasonal variation and from noise?
ideas.estimand: trend per unit time; seasonal amplitude; breakpoint date and pre/post difference

analysis.method: decomposition (trend/seasonal/residual), segmented regression or interrupted time series

ideas.falsification: no trend beyond seasonal variation, or the breakpoint CI includes the whole window
ideas.caveat: needs enough periods to separate trend from seasonality; with one cycle they are confounded

power.note: needs several full cycles for decomposition

ideas.title: Are there distinct profiles, and do they differ on the outcome?
ideas.question: Do the observations fall into distinct multivariate profiles (not just a continuous gradient), and do those profiles differ on post_score in a way that would change how they are handled?
ideas.estimand: number and size of profiles; between-profile difference in the outcome

analysis.method: k-means/mixture with k by silhouette, bootstrap stability, then outcome association out-of-sample

ideas.falsification: silhouette < .30 or bootstrap ARI < .60 (segments are not stable)
ideas.caveat: a clustering is a description until it predicts something outside the clustering variables
assumption_risks: education has few integer levels: decide ordinal vs continuous explicitly

dropped.title: any idea using a derived score as a mediator, moderator or predictor
dropped.why: change_score is mathematically derived from the outcome (flagged by the redundancy scan); using it as a predictor of that outcome is a tautology, not a mechanism
